summary: Full-size, first-party reviewed product face inside the authenticated Dual wallet. Uses the existing dual.face.bridge v1 envelope, handshake and limits; adds a programme ('application') context variant and named capability modules. No second postMessage protocol, no generic fetch/proxy/token operation.

contextVariants.application: new; sent ONLY to a product-application binding; object_id and object are null

applicationBinding.source: wallet server-only registry PRODUCT_FACE_APPLICATIONS (JSON array); resolved by an authenticated wallet BFF route, never from face, object custom data or URL

fields.origin: exact https origin (http only for loopback outside production)
fields.artifactHash: sha256:<64 hex> of the emitted artifact manifest
fields.templateIds: Dual template ids (24 hex) that belong to the programme
fields.projectionFields: public custom fields the host may project to the face, subset of [recordId,title,serialNumber,model,manufacturer,state]

applicationBinding.readyIdentity: dual.face.ready.application must be {id, version, publisher, programme, artifact, contract:'dual-product-face-v1'} and EVERY value must equal the binding exactly (version exact, not just major); mismatch closes the channel

taskPath.rule: a path segment that names a product is a hint only; the host re-selects through programme.product.select

programme.products.list.authority: wallet BFF -> api-v3 listObjects for the session wallet, filtered to binding.templateIds; server authorises person and resource

programme.product.select.authority: host re-reads getObjectById; must be owned by the session wallet AND in binding.templateIds; otherwise not_in_programme / not_owned; replaces any previous selection and invalidates its context_id

navigation.task.update.effect: host mirrors to wallet URL (push for new task, replace when same); Back/Forward and reload restore it

payload.object_id: 24 hex (Dual object of the exact unit, resolved by the runtime from handover evidence)

result.assertion: one-time wallet assertion (scope register, bound to op + object + audience)

programme.registration.authorize.authority: host reads the PUBLIC object projection, requires template in binding.templateIds and owner != session wallet; shows NATIVE confirmation with canonical facts (name, serial/model from public projection, programme, publisher, the user's own wallet); persists the operation OUTSIDE the iframe BEFORE issuing the assertion; never accepts a recipient/wallet from the face
errors: operation_already_submitted (no re-mint for an issued operation)

programme.session.assert.authority: for runtime private reads and read-only reconciliation; never authorises a write

result.readback: host canonical readback: owner == session wallet

programme.operation.status.authority: read-only; reconciles from the host journal + api-v3 readback; never retries or re-mints

session.ended.rule: host then closes the channel and removes the frame; face must drop all private state

registrationRules: Register product is the reviewed Passport first-owner handoff: owner-link grant (handover evidence) + request_transfer with the requester's own verified wallet + issuer-signed Dual transfer + exact readback.

NEVER map Register product to the Dual standard action claim_ownership (that claims an object ON CHAIN as a collectible and is not holder ownership). Neither host nor face may request claim_ownership for registration.
A serial number, login, bookmark, object id or task link is not ownership. 'Registered' requires the runtime's verified transfer readback AND the host's api-v3 readback owner == session wallet.

Cancellation before the assertion is issued = not_submitted. After issue, a lost frame/confirmation is outcome_unknown until read-only reconciliation; the original operation is retained; no blind retry, remint or replacement.
Unknown counters are null, never inferred zero.

walletAssertion.format: compact JWS, alg EdDSA (Ed25519), typ dual-face-assertion+jwt
walletAssertion.issuer: wallet BFF only (server-only signing key FACE_ASSERTION_SIGNING_KEY + FACE_ASSERTION_KEY_ID); absent key => 503 face_assertion_unprovisioned (fail closed)
claims: wallet_address (session wallet account address read server-side)
walletAssertion.verifier: Studio runtime only; keys from TIG_PRODUCT_FACE_WALLET_ASSERTION_KEYS (JSON {kid: spki PEM}) + TIG_PRODUCT_FACE_WALLET_ISSUERS; jti consumed atomically once; any mismatch refuses with zero writes
walletAssertion.gap: G1: no canonical Dual/api-v3 launch or identity contract exists for a wallet person to reach a Studio runtime. This assertion is the secure seam; production requires provisioning both keys. It is not a wallet token, refresh cookie or role session.

runtime.framing: CSP frame-ancestors = exact configured wallet origins (TIG_PRODUCT_FACE_WALLET_ORIGINS); no X-Frame-Options DENY on this route only; every other route unchanged

result.accounting: {providerWritesExecuted, dualWritesExecuted, readbacksExecuted, unknownWriteOutcomes} integer or null

POST /api/product-face/v1/registrations/.result: read-only reconcile of the durable intent/outbox; same shape

localHarness.walletE2eFaceFixture: http://localhost:4101 (pinned emitted Studio artifact + labelled fake runtime, wallet e2e only)
localHarness.studioFaceRuntime: http://localhost:4180 (actual Studio runtime + emitted artifact, scripts/product-face-harness.mjs)
localHarness.studioFakeDual: http://127.0.0.1:4011 (Studio local fake Dual, labelled; serves api-v3 shaped GET /objects/:id, GET /objects?template_id=&owner=, GET /ebus/action-logs?object_id= for programme objects)
localHarness.integratedMode: wallet mock-api forwards programme-template object reads to MOCK_PROGRAMME_DUAL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4011 so both sides read one fake Dual state

knownGaps.G1: wallet->runtime person identity/launch contract (assertion seam above; provisioning required)
knownGaps.G2: generated apps send frame-ancestors 'none' and SameSite=Strict cookies; the face uses its own versioned framable route and an in-memory face handle, not role-session cookies
knownGaps.G3: Claims pack has no info-request or quote approve/decline actions (customer: open_claim, submit_evidence, appeal_claim only)
knownGaps.G4: Passport model content has no setup/troubleshooting/manual fields; supplied as versioned face content
knownGaps.G5: no backend face-application registry; wallet uses a deployment-configured server-only registry
